tasks.short: Agree priorities, resolve design conflicts and choose solutions with management and development teams.

steps.what: Collect requests and feedback from the {PROJECT}, {EMAIL} and {DOCS}.
Assemble options, estimates and supporting evidence in the {DOCS}.
Discuss user needs, delivery constraints and conflicting preferences.
Choose priorities, content criteria and an acceptable delivery scope.
Write the decision note and agreed actions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Typed discussion notes, explicit approved priorities and content criteria.
loop.output: A draft decision note with decisions, unresolved questions, owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Require source references. Flag missing owners and dates. Check decisions against explicit approval fields.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per meeting; unresolved conflicts return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles headings, but discussion notes express agreements and qualifications in free text.

steps.what: Check the decision note and update owners, priorities and dates in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured intake in the {PROJECT} captures requests and links evidence from the {DOCS} and {BI}; a deterministic generator assembles the option pack. People negotiate and approve priorities, then a bounded drafting loop prepares the decision note. The designer checks the proposed changes before the {WORKFLOW} updates the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests and evidence were scattered, while decisions depended on negotiation. Connecting records and maintaining meeting packs often cost more than the paperwork saved.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and connectors cover intake. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the comparison pack, while a bounded model can draft notes from supplied evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Teams may disagree about value, capacity or authority. Software cannot settle those disputes or turn uncertain estimates into reliable commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Make competing interests explicit, recognise unstated concerns and negotiate a commitment people will honour.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on the highest-value customer journey obstacle to remove.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence gathering and minute writing, leaving more time for user evidence and negotiation. With explicit delegation, the designer can sequence small changes inside an approved scope; budget decisions remain with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Prioritise landing-page improvements against campaign objectives.
reach.learn: Campaign economics, capacity trade-offs and the limits of delegated spending authority.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, linked evidence and approval flows can automate coordination without automating negotiation.
Drafting a reliable decision note from supplied notes is plausible, but this digest contains no direct design-meeting case.

assumptions: This describes a marketing design team in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff; time shares are estimates.
The design review group includes relevant management, content and development roles.
Configured connectors can collect selected records and links without interpreting their meaning.
Typed notes are sufficient; recording meetings is unnecessary.
Build ranges are working effort. Access work includes privacy review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable; waiting time may extend delivery.
unknowns: Which request channels and connectors are available.
Who can approve scope, content criteria and priority changes.
Whether estimates and user evidence are recorded consistently.
Whether the proposed data processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Does structured intake reduce preparation time without excluding informal requests?
How often do draft notes misstate a decision, qualification or owner?
new_work: Check draft decision notes and proposed backlog changes.
Resolve incomplete requests and contradictory approvals.
Maintain intake fields, evidence links and access permissions.

tasks.short: Write and maintain interface manuals, testing protocols and design reports.

steps.what: Collect specifications, design files and test results from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
Choose the audience, document scope and required explanations.
Build document sections, screenshots, tables and test-result summaries in the {DOCS}.
Write instructions, explanations and limitations around the assembled evidence.

loop.input: Versioned source pack, audience, outline and document skeleton.
loop.output: A source-linked draft with instructions, explanations and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Check links, terminology and required sections automatically. Require sources for factual claims and flag unsupported instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per document; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can insert tables and headings, but audience-specific explanations require interpreting the supplied material.

steps.what: Verify technical statements and reproduce documented procedures.
Edit for audience clarity and approve the exact version for release.
Publish the approved version to the {DOCS} or {CMS} and record its location.

tasks.design: A generator assembles versioned specifications, approved screenshots and test results from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT} into standard document sections. A bounded model drafts explanations, followed by technical checking and editorial approval. The {WORKFLOW} publishes only the exact approved version to the {DOCS} or {CMS} and flags later source changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence changed across several files, and document templates could not write clear explanations. Manual copying also made documentation drift from the interface.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned exports and inexpensive generators can assemble factual sections. Bounded drafting can fill narrative sections while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented behaviour and weak source material remain expensive to resolve. Clear instructions still need someone to try the procedure and understand the audience.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a reader will misunderstand and decide which limitations must be explained prominently.

ambition.what: Role-specific interface guidance for occasional regional content editors.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time copying evidence and more time checking comprehension with readers. They can propose audience-specific guidance, but publication authority changes only if explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Design task-based help for occasional interface users.
reach.learn: Information architecture, plain-language procedures and documentation usability testing.

evidence.claim: Structured specifications and test results can populate documentation templates deterministically.
Source-grounded narrative drafting with technical review is feasible; the digest provides no direct interface-documentation case.
GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance that could help build the generator; it does not establish documentation accuracy.

assumptions: The designer writes documentation, while a developer checks implementation details.
Approved screenshots and test results can be associated with a specific interface version.
Publication uses an immutable approved version; edits invalidate its release approval.
GDPR applies to personal data in examples and screenshots. Model access and EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual deployment.
Access effort includes any required consultation under national rules; elapsed approval waits are additional.
unknowns: Which documents are public and who holds publication authority.
Whether specifications and screenshots are versioned reliably.
Whether documentation contains personal data or confidential implementation details.
Which languages, accessibility formats and retention periods are required.
research_questions: Which sections can be generated entirely from authoritative structured sources?
Can occasional readers complete a task from the generated instructions without assistance?
new_work: Review unsupported claims and reproduce important instructions.
Maintain templates, terminology and source-to-document mappings.
Resolve stale-source alerts and regenerate affected sections.
Remove personal data from screenshots and examples before drafting.

tasks.short: Create, validate and schedule interface tests across supported browsers, devices and external services.

steps.what: Inspect browser usage, interface requirements and external-service specifications.
Agree critical journeys, supported environments and acceptable coverage gaps.
Map journeys, browsers, devices and service responses in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Write test routines and simulated service responses in code-editor and source-control tools.

loop.input: Approved test matrix, interface code snapshot, test conventions and synthetic service fixtures.
loop.output: A proposed test-code change linked to matrix cases.
loop.check: Check syntax, fixture schemas, required assertions and matrix coverage. Execute in an isolated test environment.
loop.stop: At most three generate-and-check attempts per batch; failures return to a developer. Never weaken assertions or approve changed baselines automatically.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable journeys use deterministic templates; new interaction sequences require interpreting interface code and expected behaviour.

steps.what: Run routines across environments using browser-testing tools and inspect failures.
Review test adequacy, investigate failures and approve routines for the shared suite.
Set recurring runs in test-scheduling tools and document coverage in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A deterministic job combines aggregate usage from the {BI} with approved support requirements in the {DOCS} to generate a test matrix and fixtures. Existing testing tools in the {OTHER} slot run template-based tests, while a bounded model drafts unfamiliar routines in an isolated branch. A developer approves additions to the shared suite; configured schedules send results to the {PROJECT} and generate the testing protocol in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Browser matrices and external-service fixtures required repeated manual setup. New interface flows also needed custom test code and careful maintenance.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured test runners already cover repeat execution. AI-assisted coding and bounded test generation can reduce the effort of creating missing routines.
tasks.still_hard: Passing tests do not prove that the right behaviour was tested. Real-device quirks, unstable services, accessibility and unrealistic fixtures still require specialist investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Identify missing failure modes and distinguish a product defect from a misleading test.

ambition.what: An on-demand compatibility check for campaign preview pages.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time maintaining matrices and rerunning routine checks, and more time exploring risky journeys. They can recommend browser support changes from evidence; acceptance of coverage gaps remains with the development lead.

reach.task: Check campaign landing pages for rendering and conversion-path failures.
reach.learn: Search rendering, consent-dependent attribution and campaign conversion measurement.

evidence.claim: Playwright Test Agents can generate test plans and tests and attempt repairs. This supports bounded test drafting, not automatic acceptance of coverage.
GitHub Copilot supports code generation and review with human oversight.
Configured runners, deterministic matrices and synthetic fixtures can handle routine execution.

assumptions: Some browser tests exist, but a spreadsheet still tracks gaps and supported combinations.
The {OTHER} slot covers code-editor, source-control, browser-testing and test-scheduling tools.
Tests use isolated environments and synthetic data, without production payment or messaging actions.
Usage inputs are aggregated. GDPR and national consultation requirements must be assessed if identifiable visitor or employee data is introduced.
Access ranges include privacy review and any applicable employee consultation effort; external waiting time is additional.
unknowns: Which browsers, real devices and assistive technologies are formally supported.
Whether external services offer usable sandboxes and stable interface specifications.
How much of the existing test suite is reliable.
Who can approve suite changes and accepted coverage gaps.
Which testing infrastructure and aggregate analytics are accessible.
research_questions: Do generated tests detect deliberately introduced interaction and service-response faults?
Which checks require real devices or manual assistive-technology testing?
What share of failures comes from test instability rather than product defects?
new_work: Review proposed routines, assertions and fixture realism.
Investigate failures and maintain selectors and supported-environment rules.
Review visual baseline changes and browser-version updates.
Maintain isolated test accounts and external-service fixtures.

tasks.short: Design site structures, interaction models and reusable image or page templates.

steps.what: Inspect existing pages, navigation and content types in the {CMS}.
Interpret user research, project goals, brand guidance and accessibility requirements.
Create the sitemap and interaction model using interface-design tools.
Compose image and page templates using interface-design tools.
Build a responsive preview in the {CMS} and check layout rules.
Observe users navigating the preview and discuss problems with stakeholders.
Choose required revisions and approve the design package for implementation.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {CMS} produce a content inventory, while reusable components in interface-design tools under {OTHER} reduce drawing and layout work. A deterministic generator assembles template variants from approved components, image rules and content schemas; the {CMS} creates private responsive previews. The designer shapes navigation and visual hierarchy, tests comprehension with users and submits the design package for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content inventories and template variants were repeatedly rebuilt by hand. Component libraries helped, but connecting design rules to content schemas required custom work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing component and preview features cover much of the workflow. AI-assisted coding can make a small schema-to-template generator cheaper to build and adjust.
tasks.still_hard: Weak user research, missing reusable components and unusual content can make generation ineffective. Navigation, visual hierarchy and accessibility still need contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Find an organising idea that matches users' mental models and express it through coherent visual and interaction choices.

ambition.what: A content-editor template playground with realistic content and responsive previews.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time inventorying pages and reproducing layouts, and more time testing alternative structures with users. With delegated authority, they can approve component-level variations within brand and accessibility constraints; major navigation changes still need design-lead approval.

reach.task: Define reusable page structures that fit real editorial content.
reach.learn: Content modelling, editorial workflows and testing with long, missing or translated content.

reach.task: Specify reusable image treatments for responsive templates.
reach.learn: Art direction, image rights and crop rules across viewport sizes.

evidence.claim: Reusable components, structured content and configured previews can reduce repetitive template production.
GitHub Copilot can assist implementation of template generators; the source does not establish design quality.
A developer field study reported more completed tasks with coding assistance, but this does not establish a comparable gain for interface design.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slot represents interface-design tools.
The {CMS} provides content exports and private previews.
An initial component library exists; creating a complete design system is outside these build ranges.
Generation uses approved images and rule-based crops rather than inventing new artwork.
GDPR applies to user research. EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual AI use; consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Access ranges include applicable privacy and consultation effort; elapsed waiting time is additional.
unknowns: How complete and consistent the component library and content schema are.
Whether the design tools and {CMS} support the required exports and imports.
Which accessibility, language and image-rights requirements apply.
Who can approve template variations and navigation changes.
Whether representative users and realistic content are available for testing.
research_questions: Which template families can be generated without reducing useful design variation?
Do proposed structures improve findability in observed user tasks?
Where do long text, translation, zoom and missing images break generated layouts?
new_work: Review generated variants and refine visual hierarchy.
Maintain component mappings, content schemas and image rules.
Test extreme content, responsive behaviour and accessibility.
Retire outdated templates and incorporate findings from editor use.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward understanding users, shaping interaction choices and validating outcomes. Repetitive assembly, documentation and test execution shrink; wider decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Work with marketing managers on evidence-based landing-page priorities.
Work with technical writers on task-based interface guidance.
Work with search marketing strategists on rendering and conversion-path quality.
Work with editors and graphic designers on reusable content and image structures.
skills_to_grow: Content modelling and reusable component design.
Deterministic generation and practical system integration.
Browser-test coverage, realistic fixtures and failure diagnosis.
Accessibility evaluation and observed usability testing.
Negotiation, campaign measurement and delegated decision-making.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a small interface improvement service: turn a campaign brief into testable page options, compatibility evidence and editor guidance. Measure user task success and delivery effort before expanding; the digest does not justify assuming a 10-to-100-fold productivity gain.
